args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in production in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc had only been healthy in staging, so it did not qualify.) After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with an error rate of 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2). The service is healthy again.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks, with an error rate of 18%.
- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc came later but was only ever healthy in staging, so it didn't count. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before, so the change-manager approval rule didn't apply.
- **After:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging).
